subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: When compaction itself fails because a local provider rejects the summarization request, should OpenClaw keep manual blocked recovery, persist an explicit failed-compaction marker, try a configured fallback/alternate compaction model, or auto-rotate/replay once?
rationale: The current behavior is real and source-backed, but the safest recovery semantics cross session continuity, provider routing, config-surface, and replay-safety boundaries; automation should not choose that policy from one MLX failure mode.

options.title: Persist failed-compaction state first
options.body: Add a durable session marker and user/operator recovery affordance for failed compaction while keeping automatic replay out of the first fix.

options.title: Fallback to another compaction route
options.body: Define and test how failed compaction may use an existing fallback or explicit compaction model without adding provider-specific thread settings.

options.title: Guarded rotate and replay
options.body: Allow a one-shot rotation/replay only with explicit replay-safety gates, loop caps, and docs for side-effect risk.

recommendation.title: Persist failed-compaction state first
recommendation.body: Add a durable session marker and user/operator recovery affordance for failed compaction while keeping automatic replay out of the first fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about core session recovery semantics and durable state shape, and this person has the strongest available routing signal from adjacent session-state and policy history.
